ls_ferryhand.text: The boat for Kirkwall, and on to Aberdeen. Overnight, the old way: cabin, a hot breakfast and a sea that has views. Hold on to your hat, and your dinner, and sometimes both.

ls_harbour_hand.text: Bressay's just across the sound there. The harbour's sheltered by it, which is why Lerwick is here at all. The Dutch herring fleets used to anchor in the sound by the hundred, and the town grew up selling them things.
Mind you don't say 'Shetland Islands' to anyone local who's feeling prickly. 'Shetland' is fine. 'The Shetlands' makes some folk wince, though most are too polite to say.

ls_dialect.text: Shetland dialect is half Scots and half Norse. A 'peerie' thing is a small thing. A 'voe' is a sea inlet, from the Norse. A 'böd' is an old fishing store. A 'ness' is a headland. If you hear 'da' it means 'the', and you're to nod.
The northern lights we call the mirrie dancers. Some say they dance on the ice at the edge of the world. Others say it's the weather. I prefer the dancing.

then.text: Is that a Fair Isle? Properly done, too. Who knitted it? Hand it here, I'll check the steeks.

ls_knitter.text: I knit Fair Isle. Two colours a row, no more. It's the carrying of the yarn that does you in, not the knitting. Knit in the round and you've no seams. The old fishermen's jerseys were done that way so there was nothing to rub.
There's a story that the pattern was borrowed from Spanish sailors from a wrecked Armada ship in 1588. It's a nice story. The experts are not convinced.

ls_birder.text: Puffins at Sumburgh Head from May to August, if you're patient, and quiet, and a bit lucky. Then they vanish out to sea for the winter and nobody knows quite where. Arctic terns will dive-bomb you at the nest. Wear a hat. Wear a thick hat.
Shetland has a wren, the Shetland wren, that's a bit bigger and louder than the mainland one. It lives on the cliffs. I think it's smug.

ls_pier_kid.text: We get a day off for Up Helly Aa. Mum says it's because everyone's been up all night. I say it's because they burned a ship.
My da's in the Jarl Squad this year. He's grown a beard for it. Mum wants it gone. They've been to counselling.

arc_guizer.text: The squads have added a verse for the Roll of the Isles. We do it at the Town Hall after the Jarl's address, and the galley burns as ever. Nobody told the galley about the new verse.
We will be at the Douglas Gathering in July, mind. The torches are staying home. The Manx have a bylaw.
